audit.whatIsWrong: Three places claim 5 Hemorrhage stacks reset Noxian Guillotine's cooldown (spikes[2].text, whys[4], mid, wants.foe[1]).
audit.why: Riot's own text: 'If Noxian Guillotine is a killing blow, its cooldown is refreshed for a brief duration.' Five Hemorrhage stacks enrage Darius for bonus AD and raise R's damage; they do not touch its cooldown. A Mel player who believes the reset is stack-gated will misread the single most dangerous timer in the lane.
audit.corrected: Noxian Guillotine refreshes only on a killing blow; 5 stacks enrage him and raise R's damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing cues. breakdown.cooldowns said 'Count it out loud if you must' without ever giving the number.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 falling to 16s at rank 5 — the whole matchup is whether it is up. Decimate is 9s to 5s. Mel's own Rebuttal is 38s at rank 1, not the ~20s the trading text implied.
audit.corrected: Stated the real Apprehend 26s/16s band, Decimate 9s-5s, and Rebuttal 38s at rank 1, with an explicit 'step up only after Apprehend whiffs' cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.trading claimed Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds' after a bad cast.
audit.why: Rebuttal's cooldown is 38/35/33/29/26. At the ranks this matchup is decided (1-2) it is 38s or 35s — nearly double the stated figure, which makes a wasted W far more punishing than the text implies.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5].t and the interaction text only repeated 'bait the pull'; the actual Rebuttal-versus-Guillotine interaction was never stated.
audit.why: Rebuttal prevents Mel from taking damage outright, and Noxian Guillotine is a 460-range leap with a visible commit. That is the one defensive answer Mel has to R, and it is a timing problem, not a positioning one. Solar Snare buys distance but Apprehend still reaches 535 on a rooted target.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal's damage prevention is what refuses the Guillotine leap; Solar Snare only buys the distance.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere said where Darius's lane sustain comes from.
audit.why: Decimate heals Darius only off enemy champions and large monsters struck by the outer blade — minions give him nothing. A Mel who never lets the blade clip her removes his entire lane sustain, which reframes the anti-heal item timing flagged in _missing-interactions as a poke-discipline problem first.
audit.corrected: Every Decimate blade that clips you heals him; poke range starves his sustain outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this FAVOURED at 4/10 with all seven phases scored for Mel at 7-8/10, while the content layer gives Darius five of seven stages and the matchup sits at 40% over 15 games.
audit.why: The two layers tell a Mel player opposite things about the same lane. The content layer matches the win rate; the full layer is untouched boilerplate.
audit.corrected: Full layer should read UNFAVOURED with Darius holding levels 2-6. Could not be proposed: diff, diffRating, phases[].side and phases[].rating are templated strings shared across 18-315 other matchups, so the applier rejects them as ambiguous.

edits.after: The lane flips — Apprehend (26s at rank 1) drags you into Decimate range and starts Hemorrhage bleed that keeps ticking as you walk away.

edits.after: Darius's biggest threat window: Noxian Guillotine refreshes only on a killing blow, so bank Solar Snare's root to break the 460-range leap, not to open a trade.

edits.after: Noxian Guillotine refreshes on kills, so one E-pull into 5 Hemorrhage stacks feeds a true-damage execute your root can't answer.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are his lane, not yours — your Q ranks and Overwhelm stacks mean nothing if he's never out of E range to take the poke. He wins essentially every melee all-in from 1 to 9, so the game is: hug your turret, last-hit at max Radiant Volley range, and treat Solar Snare as a panic-disengage, not a trade tool. At 6 his Noxian Guillotine resets on 5 Hemorrhage stacks, so a single E-pull can become two executes in one fight — your root and W shield exist only to survive that, not to win it.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are his lane, not yours — your Q ranks and Overwhelm stacks mean nothing if he's never out of E range to take the poke. He wins essentially every melee all-in from 1 to 9, so the game is: hug your turret, last-hit at max Radiant Volley range, and treat Solar Snare as a panic-disengage, not a trade tool. Apprehend is 26s at rank 1: the moment it whiffs you own roughly twenty seconds of free Q poke, and that is the only window worth stepping up in. At 6, wait for it to be down before you commit anything.

edits.before: Darius wins by landing Apprehend (Pull), denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Darius wins by landing Apprehend, dragging you into Decimate range, and stacking Hemorrhage to five before your execute math matures.

edits.before: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — once he's marked deep, your execute math starts working. Track Apprehend (Pull) before stepping up.
edits.after: Stack Overwhelm from max range only — step up after Apprehend whiffs, never before. His five-stack enrage ends any trade you're still in.

edits.before: - Darius Apprehend (Pull): matchup-defining — The pull starts every Darius kill pattern — bait it before stepping up. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Darius Apprehend: 26s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — it is the whole matchup. Bait it and you own the next twenty seconds. - Decimate: 9s down to 5s, and it heals him only off the champions his outer blade clips. - Your Rebuttal: 38s at rank 1.

Bad trade: Burning Rebuttal on chip damage and then standing in Apprehend (Pull) range — your only defensive layer is gone for twenty seconds.
edits.after: Good trade: snare him on his farming spot, fan two full Q volleys while he's locked, and step back before Apprehend's 26 seconds are back up. Bad trade: burning Rebuttal on chip damage and then standing in Apprehend (Pull) range — your only defensive layer is gone for 38 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: That is Darius’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 — inside that window he owns you, outside it he cannot start.

edits.before: Track Darius’s Apprehend (Pull): The pull starts every Darius kill pattern — bait it before stepping up. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.

notes: Full-layer verdict fields are stale boilerplate and could not be corrected through the applier: diff ('FAVOURED', 18 shared copies), diffRating ('4/10', 54), carryRating (315), and every phases[].side/.rating (153-240 copies each) are byte-identical across matchups, so the applier's exactly-once rule rejects them. The full layer therefore still scores Mel 7-8/10 in all seven phases of a 40%-win-rate lane while the content layer correctly gives Darius levels 2-6. This needs a structural fix outside the proposal flow. Also left alone deliberately: 'Solar Snare's 1.5s root' and the '550-range auto' figure used 37 times across mel.js — neither Mel's root duration nor her attack range is on disk (the kit file carries no stats block), so I could not verify either and did not touch them.
